issues.problem: Both candidate CLIs reach Budget.reserve for an unregistered --split holdout run. Shared ledger path resolves against process.cwd(); inherited Budget initializes absent ledger to zero. Therefore direct candidate CLI invocation alone does not establish prospective admission or the authoritative existing shared spend ledger.

reproduction.method: Budget.prototype.reserve replaced temporarily in memory with a throwing sentinel; two CLI calls reached it with cap75 and a nonexistent CWD-local ledger. Reserve restored afterward; no actual reservation/provider/defaultTransport/auth read, no held-out model response or inference.

issues.recommendation: Before paid admission, add a separately registered candidate controller with committed source/prompt/model/task hashes, exact frozen byte verification, canonical existing ledger/cap/remaining-plan affordability and separately released holdout gates. Make it the sole approved dispatch entry, or require an explicit candidate admission object and canonical existing ledger in each CLI before reserve. Keep exported injected runners available for isolated source tests.

limitations: No new native API response or model ability validation; mock payload proof is not provider admission.
